events.title: Comics of Care: Healing Through Graphic Medicine
events.venue: Sally T. WongAvery Library, 3100 Biomedical Sciences Wy La Jolla, CA 92093
events.description: What role can art and storytelling play in understanding health — and in healing? Explore comics, graphic novels and memoirs from UC San Diego Library's Graphic Medicine Collection: vividly drawn, personal stories about the experience of facing illness and finding care. In these pages, a single drawing can capture what's hard to put into words, sharing insights we can see and feel. We can learn from those who've faced health challenges and witness how they found their way through. Comics of Care is presented in connection with The Science of Story, a signature celebration of storytelling across UC San Diego. Returning for a third year during Comic-Con week, this series explores the art, craft and cultural power of narrative. In joining that conversation, this book exhibit shows how art and stories can help us heal — by letting us into another person's experience of illness and recovery. We hope these works deepen empathy for health struggles and spark discussion among patients, caregivers and clinicians who want to improve care. This collection was curated by UC San Diego librarians Jeffery Loo, Karen Heskett and Zemirah Ngow. Comics of Care is on view in the Sally T. WongAvery Library breezeway from June 29 to September 13, during the building's open hours.

events.title: Concerts on the Green 2026
events.description: Concerts on the Green (CotG) at Kate Sessions Park in the Mission Bay / Pacific Beach area provides a free contemporary musical experience to San Diego residents and visitors alike. Kate Sessions Park offers a natural amphitheater hillside where, with a stage centered at the bottom of the hill, the audience enjoys scenic views of downtown San Diego and Mission Bay Park. The Sunday four-part concert series begins in July and concludes in August, and it provides an excellent opportunity for local musicians to perform for a massive audience. Talent featured in the concerts is selected to reflect the range and diversity that San Diego has to offer. The program includes reggae, 80s yacht rock, hip hop, and anything in between! The PB Town Council also strives to be equitable in talent selection and is committed to including musical groups from within SDs Promise Zone of economically disadvantaged communities.

events.title: Shark Summer at Birch Aquarium
events.description: Have you ever wondered what species swim in our local waters? Or wanted to know what makes sharks such unique animals? This July, join us as we dive deep into the world of these amazing animals, with fin-tastic fun for shark fans of all ages! Shark Summer celebrates the vital role sharks play in the ecosystem, while shining a light on the important conservation work and research being done to protect them.

events.title: 25th Annual Paper Theatre Festival | Exhibition
events.venue: Geisel Library, 9701 Hopkins Drive, La Jolla, CA 92093
events.description: UC San Diego Library’s 25th anniversary season of Paper Theatre Festival returns this summer! Join us for a unique browsing opportunity at this year’s festival, which is taking the form of a colorful exhibition of paper theatres. Located on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library in The Nest, this display is free and open to the public. Explore at your leisure from July 14 through September 27, 2026, during the building's open hours. If you need assistance or would like an informal, pop-up performance in front of the exhibition on a prearranged date and time, contact exhibition curator Scott Paulson at spaulson@ucsd.edu. Additional Information Annual Paper Theatre Festival: It’s the Smallest Show on Earth! Paper theatre, also known as tabletop or toy theatre, dates back to Victorian-era London. Families would re-enact plays they saw in miniature by cutting and pasting souvenir poster kits purchased from local playhouses. These kits included scenery sheets, costumed paper dolls and condensed scripts. This vintage marketing tool and educational toy is making a comeback!UC San Diego Library plays a featured role in reviving this artful and educational hobby. On display are 25 seasons’ worth of miniature theatrical wonders, showcasing the enthusiastic work of our students, staff, alumni and community members.We are proud to host the oldest continually running paper theatre festival in the United States!An exhibition opening reception is scheduled for Tuesday, July 14, showcasing works from Scott Paulson '84, Rachel Almodovar, Elizabeth Hines, Carin Wallace, Anastasia Hunter, Christina Continelli, and visiting artist Nancy So Miller. Learn more about the exhibition opening reception.

events.title: Summer with Stuart Concert Series
events.venue: Varies
events.description: Join us for the second annual Summer with Stuart, a pop-up concert series at various Stuart Collection Artworks. In partnership with local chamber musicians, we're presenting six weeks of free, family-friendly summer evening programming. Thursdays, 6 - 7 pm July 2: Sun God, Series kickoff with Westwind Brass As America marks its 250th birthday, Westwind Brass celebrates with Sousa-style marches, beloved folk and hymn tunes, jazz standards, Broadway showstoppers, and Hollywood film scores, all carried unamplified across Niki de Saint Phalle’s radiant Sun God lawn. The professional brass quintet — two trumpets, French horn, trombone, and tuba — sweeps across the American story, from the concert hall to the silver screen. Think Copland’s wide-open prairie sound and the brassy swagger of big-band jazz. Roughly 60–75 minutes of joyful noise for America’s 250th. Check out the band in advance: Listen to Westwind Brass Location: Sun God in Google Maps Parking: Scholars Parking Structure in Google Maps July 9: La Jolla Project, Left Coast Quintet As dusk settles over the Richard Fleischner’s La Jolla Project, five wind players gather among UC San Diego’s popular outdoor artwork, known as “Stonehenge,” for an evening that spans centuries in a single breath. The Left Coast Quintet — flute, oboe, clarinet, French horn, and bassoon — is one of music’s most eloquent ensembles: five distinct voices, one rich palette of color. Their program moves fluidly from Baroque counterpoint and Classical-era works (the woodwind quintet was born in Mozart’s day) to Romantic showpieces, contemporary discoveries, and imaginative arrangements of jazz and film music. What sets LCQ apart is its blend of warmth, humor, and polish — as at home with a Baroque partita as a film-score medley, and always ready to let the audience in on the fun. About 60 minutes where art, landscape, and music fold into one another. Check out the band in advance: Listen to Left Coast Quintet on their website Location: La Jolla Project in Google Maps Parking: Theater District Parking Structure in Google Maps July 16: Bear, Westwind Virtuosi Westwind Virtuosi returns to the most intimate setting in the series — the Bear courtyard, centered on Tim Hawkinson's massive granite boulder, Bear, also known as "Beryl." Something happens when strings play beside that stone: the granite seems to lean in and listen, holding the sound warm and close. This chamber ensemble — violin, viola, cello, and bass — draws on the heart of the string repertoire, from Haydn and Mozart through the Romantics, favoring lyrical slow movements that reward close listening: the cello’s deep warmth, the violin’s singing upper register, the feel of private conversation between musicians. Expect folk songs, tango, and lighter classics that translate beautifully to strings in the open air. Check out the band in advance: Listed to Westwind Virtuosi on their website Location: Bear in Google Maps Parking: Gilman Parking Structure in Google Maps July 23: Sun God, Manny Cepeda + Westwind Strings & Brass We’ve never done this before — and that’s exactly the point: For one electrifying hour, strings, brass, and the irresistible Manny Cepeda come together for a brand-new program of salsa, rhythm, and pure Latin joy. Sábor means flavor, and this concert has it in abundance. Cepeda — one of San Diego’s most beloved Latin musicians — leads a combined ensemble of Westwind string and brass players through salsa, cumbia, bolero, and cha-cha: forms rooted in Cuba, Colombia, and Puerto Rico and built on syncopated rhythm and call-and-response. The strings, unusual in a Latin dance band, lend lush warmth beneath the brass’s punch and swagger — the full sound of the great Tito Puente–era orchestras. The Sun God lawn's open footprint gives the music room to move. Check out the band in advance: Listen to Manny Cepeda on his website Location: Sun God in Google Maps Parking: Scholars Parking Structure in Google Maps July 30: La Jolla Project, Hornswoggle Thirty French horns gather at dusk at the La Jolla Project— and the results are elemental. Hornswoggle is one of the few ensembles in the country performing at this scale, and the French horn genuinely sounds better outdoors than in any hall. Thirty players spread across the grounds, dispersing the sound so it surrounds you rather than faces you — hunting calls and fanfares dating to the 17th and 18th centuries, hymn-like chorales and folk songs that bloom across horns in unison, and contemporary works written for the spatial possibilities of many horns in open air. Against the backdrop of La Jolla Project, it becomes a glorious, soaring wall of brass rolling into the sky. Check out the band in advance: Listen to Hornswoggle on their website Location: La Jolla Project in Google Maps Parking: Theater District Parking Structure in Google Maps August 6: Bear, Chamber Orchestra The Second Summer with Stuart ends the only way it could — with everyone on stage, Handel in the air, and Bear hearing Water Music for the very first time. Handel wrote Water Music in 1717 to be played outdoors, from a barge on the River Thames for King George I — one of the earliest masterpieces written for the open air. Three hundred years later, the combined forces of our summer series bring it back where it belongs: beside Tim Hawkinson’s granite boulder Bear, under a summer sky. Roughly twenty musicians — strings, brass, and winds drawn from every ensemble of the season, many of them former San Diego Chamber Orchestra players — gather for the full sweep of Handel’s suites: stately overtures, graceful minuets, and spirited hornpipes. Location: Bear in Google Maps Parking: Gilman Parking Structure in Google Maps Summer with Stuart Concert Series Sharable Flyer for Printing (Google Doc) Stuart Collection: The Stuart Collection at the University of California, San Diego – comprised of 22 permanent artworks by world-renowned artists, and growing – aims to question conventional understandings of public art in playful and insightful ways through our commissioning programs, and seeks to enrich the cultural, intellectual, and scholarly life of the UC San Diego campus and local San Diego community. We enhance public life through art that encourages thoughtful deliberation, an awareness of difference, mental and physical wellbeing, and that inspires creative solutions to complex issues; and continue to commission exciting new works from the world’s most important contemporary artists through our Landmarks, Emerging Artists and Public Programs.

events.title: Can the U.S. and China Build a Stable Great-Power Relationship?
events.venue: Sanford Consortium for Regenerative Medicine, 2880 Torrey Pines Scenic Drive, La Jolla, California - 92037
events.description: In welcoming U.S. President Donald Trump to Beijing in May for a summit, Chinese President Xi Jinping sought to find an answer to the question of whether China and the U.S. would be able to overcome the Thucydides Trap and create a new paradigm of major country relations. After two days of intense conversation, the two leaders offered a tentative “yes,” proposing to create a new era of what they called “constructive strategic stability.” Following in the tradition of Susan Shirk, who insists on asking difficult questions and challenging conventional wisdom, the political scientist Graham Allison will devote this lecture to examining both the promise and the limits of that vision. 4:15 - 5:00 PM Reception on the Terrace5:00 - 6:30 PM Public Lecture in Roth Auditorium Welcome: Molly Roberts, Director, 21st Century China Center, UC San Diego School of Global Policy and Strategy Presider: Meghan O’Sullivan, Director, The Belfer Center; Jeane Kirkpatrick Professor of the Practice of International Affairs, Harvard Kennedy School Speaker: Graham Allison, Douglas Dillon Professor of Government, Harvard Kennedy School ------------------ This public lecture is organized by the 21st Century China Center (21CCC) at the UC San Diego School of Global Policy and Strategy. For more information about this and other 21CCC events, please visit china.ucsd.edu.
